dedupe_keys.name: a 2018 social accounting matrix for germany depicting waste and recycling accounts for a circular economy

description: Elshof, Luckmann and Siddig publish a 2018 social accounting matrix for Germany with explicit waste and recycling accounts. Zenodo lists a public Excel workbook and a technical paper under CC BY 4.0; only their metadata and the landing description were read. The matrix has 160 accounts, including 63 activities and 85 commodities, plus labour, capital, households, government, taxes, trade, stocks and savings. The provider says it derives from Germany’s Federal Statistical Office and balances a proto-matrix using cross-entropy with macroeconomic controls. Its inter-account flows can provide economic context or coefficients for waste-sector material-flow and multi-sector policy simulation scenarios. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this German matrix. A limitation is that a balanced social accounting matrix is an estimate, not observed waste-routing behaviour or facility-level throughput. The page does not expose workbook units, table orientation or uncertainty measures. The workbook was not downloaded, and balance totals were not reproduced.
